title: Integer and decimal to Float64 and Float32: correctly rounded
verdict: ≤ 0.5 ulp: Int64, Int128 and Decimal to Float64 and Float32
description: Int64 and Int128 to Float64 and Float32 are Rust `as` casts (through `num_traits`), which round to nearest, ties to even: ≤ 0.5 ulp, also above 2^53 and for 128-bit values.

Decimal to Float64 divides once when the unscaled value is at most 2^53 and the scale at most 22, and otherwise formats `<unscaled>e-<scale>` and parses it with Rust's correctly rounded parser; Decimal to Float32 rounds the Float64 again unless it sits exactly on a binary32 midpoint, then parses. Both correctly rounded.

Observed, 3 000 values each: 0 off the correctly rounded value for Int64, Int128 (to ±2^126) and Decimal(18, 6), (18, 17), (38, 10), (38, 30), (38, 2), to Float64 and Float32. Platform-independent. DuckDB's HUGEINT cast misses by up to 0.625 ulp where Polars's Int128 cast is exact on the same values (duckdb-ulp-casts).
reference: Casts of integers and decimals to doubles round once to nearest, ties to even (Lean's `Float.ofInt`, `Float.ofScientific`).

evidence.note: Decimal to Float32, Float64: dec128_to_f32, dec128_to_f64
dec128_to_f64: one exact division or parse_dec128; dec128_to_f32 checks the midpoint
int to float `as`: rounds to nearest, ties to even

pl.LazyFrame({'x': ints}, schema={'x': pl.Int64}).select(pl.col('x').cast(pl.Float64), …cast(pl.Float32)).collect(engine='streaming'): max 0.5000 / 0.49999 ulp, 0 of 3 000 off. The same for Int128 (±2^126): 0.5000 / 0.49998, 0 off.
pl.Series(decimals, dtype=pl.Decimal(p, s)).cast(…) for (18,6), (18,17), (38,10), (38,30), (38,2): max ≤ 0.49997 (Float64), ≤ 0.5000 (Float32) ulp, 0 off for each.

notes: Probe script ulp_probe.py (session scratchpad, not in the repository), run from python/ as `uv run --with mpmath python ulp_probe.py --n 3000 --seed 1 --out ulp.json`: about 3 000 inputs per operation and type, random and hard cases, against mpmath at 256 bits. 'bad' counts results that differ from the correctly rounded value; the max is in ulps of the result type at the exact value's binade. DuckDB runs on a table loaded from Parquet, Polars on a LazyFrame with collect(engine='streaming'), so the column kernels run. DuckDB 2.0.0 and Polars 2.1.0 (Python wheels), macOS 26.6 arm64, Python 3.12.11, mpmath 1.3.0.

Elementwise kernels are shared by the streaming and in-memory engines (polars-elem-rounding, polars-double-scalar-divisor); the probe collects with engine='streaming' on 3 000-row frames, so morsels hold more than one row and the literal paths run.
